title: Enterprise Onboarding: Integration, Escalation, Health Checks & QBR Playbook
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This playbook defines the standardized process for enterprise onboarding at Redwood Inference, covering integration steps, escalation paths, routine health checks, and materials for Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs). It is intended for Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), Support, and Engineering stakeholders who participate in enterprise onboarding and ongoing account health.

Scope:
- New enterprise customers and large migrations to Dedicated or Private deployments.
- Cross-functional activities from contract signature through the first 90 days and recurring QBR cadence.

Owner and stakeholders:
- Playbook owner: Customer Success (Onboarding Lead)
- Primary stakeholders: CSM (owner), Solutions Engineer (integration), Support (L2), Product/Engineering (feature/regression triage), Account Executive (commercial handoff)

Prerequisites (pre-kickoff checklist):
1. Contract signed and PO received.
2. Customer has completed security questionnaire and provided network details (for Dedicated/Private deployments).
3. Initial model selection and expected traffic patterns documented in Salesforce & Confluence.
4. API keys / deployment credentials provisioned and shared securely via company vault.

Onboarding phases (high level):
1) Kickoff (Week 0)
- Agenda: introductions, success criteria, timeline, security & compliance requirements, point-of-contact matrix.
- Deliverables: onboarding plan (timeline), access matrix, test dataset and example prompts.

2) Integration & QA (Weeks 1-3)
- Integration tasks: API key usage, SDK quickstart, webhook configuration, embeddings ingestion (if applicable).
- SE runbook: sample curl/pseudocode, recommended batching/timeout settings, and rate-limit handling.
- Acceptance tests: successful generation/embedding calls, correct auth, and expected latency under test load.

3) Pilot / Go-live (Weeks 3-6)
- Gradual traffic ramp with traffic safety guardrails: start at 1% traffic, increase to 25% over 48 hours, then to full traffic after stability confirmation.
- Monitoring: p95 latency, error rate, token consumption, and model quality checks.

4) Post-go-live (Days 7-90)
- Weekly check-ins until 30 days, biweekly until 90 days.
- Knowledge transfer: runbooks, escalation contacts, custom dashboards.

Escalation playbook (triage and escalation matrix):
- Severity definitions:
  - P0 / Sev0: Service down for customer affecting production (no workaround). Response: 15 minutes.
  - P1 / Sev1: Major functionality degraded with no reasonable workaround. Response: 1 hour.
  - P2 / Sev2: Partial loss or degraded performance, workaround available. Response: 4 business hours.
  - P3 / Sev3: Minor issue, feature request, or non-urgent bug. Response: 2 business days.

- Contacts and routing:
  - First-line: Support Tier 1 (ticket intake, initial troubleshooting).
  - Second-line: Solutions Engineer & Support L2 (integration or config issues).
  - Third-line: Eng On-call (runtime issues, kernel/serving regressions) - escalate via PagerDuty with alert context (service, request id, sample payload).

Escalation steps (ordered):
1. Triage in support ticket: gather logs, request id, timestamps, environment (hosted/dedicated/private), API key id, and sample request/response.
2. Reproduce problem in staging or with customer-provided sample if safe.
3. If P0/P1, notify on-call SRE and Solutions Engineering immediately and open a Slack incident channel.
4. Provide customer-facing status updates every 30 minutes for P0/P1 until resolved.
5. Post-incident: run a root cause analysis (RCA) and share with customer and internal stakeholders within 3 business days.

SLA and escalation thresholds:
- Hosted API customers: response and resolution SLA per contract; default target: P1 acknowledgement in 1 hour, initial remediation plan within 4 hours.
- Dedicated / Private: enterprise SOW defines SLA; follow contract plus this escalation flow.

Integration guide (practical steps):
- Authentication:
  - API keys are issued per-account. Use short-lived tokens for CI/CD where possible.
  - Example curl:
    curl -X POST https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/generate \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"model":"redwood-2.1","input":"Hello"}'

- Webhooks and callbacks:
  - Recommended: use TLS 1.2+, verify client certs for Private deployments.
  - Retry policy: exponential backoff with max 5 retries (initial 1s, multiplier 2).

- Recommended runtime settings for enterprise workloads:
  | Setting | Recommended value | Notes |
  |---------|-------------------|-------|
  | request_timeout | 30s | Increase for long generation jobs |
  | max_tokens | 2048 | Based on planned prompt/response size |
  | batch_size | 8-64 | Tune by model and latency requirements |

Common integration issues and workarounds:
- Authentication failures:
  - Symptom: 401 responses after credential rotation.
  - Workaround: Confirm key id in Secrets Manager and rotate client caches; issue short-lived tokens for CI.

- Excessive latency during peak traffic:
  - Symptom: p95 latency spikes > 2x baseline.
  - Workaround: enable request-level caching for common prefixes, reduce batch window, or route to a lower-latency model variant.

- Webhook delivery failures:
  - Symptom: 5xx from customer webhook endpoint.
  - Workaround: add retry with backoff and circuit-breaker; configure alerting for webhook failure rate > 1% in 5-minute window.

Known issues & workarounds (table):
| Issue ID | Symptom | Impacted area | Temporary workaround | Owner |
| ISSUE-2026-011 | Token cache growth causing OOM on older runtime nodes | eng-serving-runtime | Trigger cache prune and roll nodes to v1.12.3 | Runtime team |
| ISSUE-2026-032 | Webhook timeouts for Private deployments behind firewall | integration | Increase webhook timeout and deploy a small retry proxy inside customer network | SE team |
| ISSUE-2026-045 | Intermittent 429s on dedicated pools during overnight backups | capacity | Schedule backups to off-peak window, enable burst capacity for 2h | SRE/Capacity |

Support process and ticket lifecycle:
- Intake: Tickets created via support portal, email, or API. Assign severity and primary owner within 30 minutes.
- Diagnosis: Support Tier 1 collects reproducible example and logs; escalate to SE/L2 if configuration or integration related.
- Engineering triage: For suspected product/regression issues, open an internal engineering bug with reproducible steps and attach relevant traces and logs.
- Communication: Always include timeline expectations and next update time in the ticket.

Health checks and monitoring (recommended dashboards & alerts):
Key metrics to track for each customer and route:
- p50/p95/p99 latency (target p95 < 300ms for low-latency tiers)
- Error rate (target < 0.1% errors per 5m window)
- Token usage and cost-per-1K tokens trend
- Cache hit rate and batching efficiency
- Availability (target 99.9% for Dedicated SLA)

Suggested dashboards (internal names):
- Dashboard: CS / Customer X Onboarding Health (metrics: latency, errors, tokens, webhook failures)
- Dashboard: Platform / Model / redwood-2.1 / per-customer latency

Alerting examples:
- Alert: customer-api-error-rate-high -> trigger when error rate > 0.5% for 5 minutes.
- Alert: p95-latency-spike -> trigger when p95 increases by > 2x baseline for 10 minutes.

QBR materials and cadence:
- QBR frequency: Quarterly (post 90-day onboarding, then quarterly).
- Standard QBR agenda:
  1. Review objectives and success criteria (CSM)
  2. Usage and cost overview (Finance/CS)
  3. Latency, availability, and incidents since last QBR (SRE)
  4. Model quality & eval results (Applied ML)
  5. Roadmap and upcoming changes (Product)
  6. Action items and owners

- Required QBR slides and artifacts:
  - Executive summary (1 slide)
  - Key metrics dashboard (screenshots + query links)
  - Incident summary and RCA highlights (if any)
  - Cost optimization recommendations (batching, quantization, routing policy)

Operational checklists and runbooks (links to short runbooks):
- Onboarding runbook: step-by-step integration tests, smoke checks, and post-rollout verification.
- Incident runbook: customer-facing incident updates template and RCA template.
- Capacity runbook: instructions for enabling burst capacity and scaling dedicated pools.

Postmortem and continuous improvement:
- For any Sev1/Sev0 affecting a customer during onboarding, run a joint RCA with customer stakeholders and identify 3 measurable action items. Publish internal RCA within 3 business days and follow up during next weekly sync until resolved.

Appendices:
A. Handoff checklist (CS -> Support): list of artifacts to hand off after 90 days.
B. Template emails and Slack channels (examples).
C. Escalation contact table: role, name, PagerDuty escalation policy id (internal).
